text:
maria: Quick thread to land design for the new synthetic traffic generator (codename: surgewave). Goal: produce reproducible microbursts + long-tail latency shapes we can use for apples-to-apples kernel/batching/regression tests.

ajay: love the name. what are the hard requirements?

maria: minimal set: deterministic seeds, configurable QPS ramp shapes (linear, sawtooth, poisson bursts), per-client KV warmup behavior, prefix-cache-aware replay, and exact token-level timing for kernel comparisons.

lex: can we keep it small initially? a single-process harness that emits HTTP requests with specified inter-arrival distributions is fine. later we can parallelize for cluster runs.

toni: important: generator must be able to pin model variant and kernel selection so we can run the same trace with different kernels/quantization and compare tail latencies. also need stable KV cache priming sequences.

sam: +1. for KV warmup we should support: cold, partial-warm (X% prefetched), and hot. impl idea: a two-phase run: priming phase with deterministic prefixes, then measured phase that replays the same keys.

maria: sketch of config payload (proto):

```json
{
  "seed": 12345,
  "clients": 200,
  "shape": "sawtooth",
  "period_s": 300,
  "burst_profile": {"type":"poisson_mixture","lambda_peak":1200,"lambda_base":40,"burst_duration_ms":350},
  "kv_warmup": {"mode":"partial","fraction":0.25,"prefixes_per_client":8},
  "kernel_pin": "auto|flash-attn-v2|generic",
  "warmup_seconds": 60,
  "measure_seconds": 600
}
```

ajay: nice. a couple of notes: (1) include an explicit request pacing map so we can test queued vs continuous QPS; (2) allow per-request sequence length distribution — short/medium/long mix.

lex: for batching heuristic experiments we need to emit timestamps at token-level granularity in the trace so offline batch-simulator can reconstruct exact queueing behavior. include `client_send_ts`, `server_recv_offset_ms`, `tokens_expected`.

toni: on metrics: collect p50/p90/p95/p99/p999 for both generation latency and kernel exec time, plus batch sizes histogram, KV hit ratio over time, queue_time distribution, and GPU SM utilization samples. bench-bot: will emit a minimal prom endpoint during runs.

bench-bot: reminder: use same hardware profile for apples-to-apples — config field `hardware_profile` must match cluster node types and driver versions.

sam: regression workflow idea: when CI detects a perf regression, capture the failing trace and re-run through surgewave with the pinned kernel versions + previous-good kernel. that produced the delta we can attribute to kernel or batching changes.

maria: def. also add a `trace_compare` mode that runs two pinned kernels back-to-back on the same node pool and produces a diff report (latency by quantile, batch size shift, kv-hit delta).

ajay: about randomness — ensure config uses deterministic pseudo-random for inter-arrival times but also support a non-deterministic live mode for stress runs. store the seed in trace header.

lex: logging: compact single-line events to keep traces small. format: `TS | client_id | req_id | seq_len | send_offset | recv_ts | kernel | batch_size | kv_hit`. easy to parse.

toni: we should also include a minimal warmup scheduler to prime kernel caches (JIT/compilation) before measurements to avoid one-off compilation spikes. config flag `skip_jit_warmup=false`.

maria: open question: what default burst shape best matches prod? we have historical traces but they vary. suggestion: default = mixed sawtooth + poisson spikes tuned from last 3 weeks of real traffic.

sam: agree. can add presets: `prod-weekly`, `interactive`, `enterprise-batch`.

ajay: action items: I can prototype generator CLI and JSON schema. lex will add trace token-level format and offline batch simulator hook. toni will write KV warmup modes and priming runner. maria will own apples-to-apples diff report spec. bench-bot will stub endpoints.

maria: timeline? two-week spike to get a working prototype for kernel experiments. keep issues small.

lex: small nit: include `max_latency_ms` kill switch so a runaway synthetic run doesn't overload infra.

toni: acked. also add `drop_rate` to simulate transient network loss.

maria: great. I'll create a GH epic and link the initial RFC. posting the prod-derived sample config in the epic. thanks folks :rocket:

ajay: thanks — excited to see how surgewave helps isolate batching vs kernel impacts.

bench-bot: test run scheduled: 2468109999. use `--seed 12345` for reproducibility.
